DATE: Monday, October 5, 2026

SUBJECT: EXPEDITED MULTI-AGENCY FOIA REQUEST: Transcripts, Calendar Invites, and Metadata Logs for the October 1, 2026 Virtual Meeting Regarding Square 5815

Pursuant to the federal Freedom of Information Act (5 U.S.C. § 552) and the District of Columbia Freedom of Information Act (D.C. Official Code § 2-531 et seq.), I hereby request expedited production of the following public records:

NARRATIVE CONTEXT & PRIOR KNOWLEDGE:
On Sunday, October 4, 2026, NPS Superintendent Serena Bellew confirmed in writing that a multi-agency virtual meeting was held on Thursday, October 1, 2026, between the National Park Service (NPS), the Department of Energy and Environment (DOEE), and DC Water. Superintendent Bellew stated: "NPS, DC Water and DOEE had a virtual meeting last Thursday to coordinate next steps for addressing the elevated/exposed manhole cover/pipe on the site... DC Water explained that the pipe appears to be collapsed and blocked which is contributing to the water pooling."

Because this meeting involves federal and municipal agencies coordinating a response to an active infrastructure collapse, an unpermitted MS4 discharge, and biological contamination on​ a federal parkland​ swamp, I request the following records:

1. VIRTUAL MEETING PLATFORM RECORDS (Teams/Zoom/WebEx):
All digital records generated by the virtual meeting platform used to host the October 1, 2026 meeting. This specifically includes:
   - The auto-generated meeting transcript.
   - The audio/video recording of the meeting (if captured).
   - All in-meeting chat logs or instant messages sent between participants.
   - The complete digital attendee log showing the names, email addresses, and exact login/logout timestamps for every federal and municipal employee who joined the call.

2. CALENDAR METADATA & INVITATIONS:
The complete Microsoft Outlook, Google Workspace, or internal calendar invitation file (.ics or native format) for the October 1, 2026 meeting. This must include:
   - The original meeting description and agenda.
   - The complete list of invited attendees.
   - The RSVP metadata (Accepted/Declined/Tentative) for all invited federal and municipal personnel.

3. INTERNAL COORDINATION EMAILS:
All emails sent between NPS, DOEE, and DC Water personnel between September 28, 2026, and October 2, 2026, that contain the virtual meeting link, agenda, or subsequent follow-up action items resulting from the October 1 meeting.

4. HANDWRITTEN & DIGITAL NOTES:
All handwritten notes, digital notepad files, internal memos, or summaries created by Superintendent Bellew, Director Jackson, CEO Gadis, or their respective staff members during or immediately following the October 1 meeting, specifically concerning DC Water's admission of the "collapsed and blocked" pipe.

NATIVE FORMAT & METADATA PRESERVATION DEMAND:
Produce all electronic records in their native digital formats with all rich metadata intact. Do not "flatten" calendar invites or platform logs to PDF if such conversion destroys the underlying digital forensic metadata.

REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED PROCESSING:
Expedited processing is requested because there is an urgency to inform the public concerning actual government activity involving an active structural landslide and an uncontained public health biohazard adjacent to a designated public school pedestrian route.

REQUEST FOR FEE WAIVER:
Disclosure of the requested records is in the public interest because it will contribute significantly to public understanding of municipal infrastructure management, federal regulatory compliance, and inter-agency oversight of the Clean Water Act. As a community representative, I do not seek these records for commercial purposes.

Please see the attached PDF copy of this request for your administrative files.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

FRED GAMBLE JR

1. The Police Traffic Crash Report for the incident, with any supplements, diagrams, and narrative sheets. If PSP contends crash reports must be requested through its separatecrash-report process, please say so in writing within the Section 901 period and forward this item there.

2. Any incident, case, or supplemental report summarizing the incident, and any record showing the case number, assigned troopers or station, and the case's status (open, closed, or reopened).

3. Any property receipt, inventory, or evidence log listing the personal effects and clothing found on or with the unidentified female decedent (including the necklace, key chain with engraved tag, keys, and miniature padlock).

4. Photographs of those personal effects and clothing, and photographs of the scene and wreckage that do not depict the decedent's body.

5. The police sketch of the decedent and each distinct flyer, bulletin, or press release PSP has issued about her from 1986 to the present, including PSP's 2024 and 2025 public releases. Duplicates are not needed.

6. Any coroner's report, inquest notice, inquest verdict, or return from the Fayette County Coroner that is held in the PSP file (the 1986 coroner was Phillip Reilly), excluding autopsy records.

7. Administrative records of the decedent's disposition and burial, and of her June 2025 exhumation: any release-of-remains or burial authorization, the exhumation order or
permit, transfer documents to the Indiana County Coroner's Office, and any agreement or grant paperwork with the Florida Institute of Forensic Anthropology and Applied Science (IFAAS).

8. Records sufficient to show the date(s) on which the decedent was entered into the NCIC Unidentified Person File and NamUs (UP16509).

9. The case-file index or table of contents, if one exists, and the records-retention schedule that applies to this file. If any part of the file has been destroyed, archived, or transferred (for example, to the State Archives), the disposal or transfer record showing what and when.

Records I Am Not Requesting:

To narrow any dispute, this request does not seek:

• autopsy records or photographs of the body (65 P.S. § 67.708(b)(20));

• NCIC or CLEAN queries, transmissions, or hit results;

• fingerprint, dental, DNA, or laboratory data;

• contact information for living witnesses, or criminal history record information.

Exemptions, Redaction, and Discretionary Release:

If PSP believes part of a responsive record is exempt, please redact that part under Section 706 and release the rest, rather than withholding the whole record. PSP bears the burden of proving any exemption by a preponderance of the evidence (Section 708(a)(1)). Under Pennsylvania State Police v. Grove, 161 A.3d 877 (Pa. 2017), a record's connection to an investigation does not by itself make it exempt under Section 708(b)(16) or the Criminal History Record Information Act; only content that is itself investigative, such as witness interviews, evidence collection, measurements, or analysis, is protected.

The sketch, physical description, and photographs of the decedent's belongings are already public through PSP's own releases and NamUs UP16509, so releasing the same material cannotmharm the investigation. Both the driver and the passenger died in the crash. If PSP nonetheless invokes Section 708(b)(16) or (17) or CHRIA, please identify the investigation relied on and the legal basis.

To the extent a record is exempt only under Section 708, and its release is not prohibited by other law, I ask PSP to exercise its discretion under Section 506(c) to release it. PSP has publicly sought the community's help identifying this woman, and access to these records serves that effort.

communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the New York Freedom of Information Law, I hereby request the following records:

Records related to the department’s Flock Safety system:

1. Organization Audit in Flock.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Organization Audit report and corresponding retained audit records of searches conducted by users within the Department's organization. Per Flock's documentation, the Organization Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches done within the agency.

2. Network Audit in Flock.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Network Audit report and corresponding retained audit records of searches of the Department's Flock network by any agency in the Flock system. Per Flock's documentation, the Network Audit is available within the Insights tab and is defined as searches of the organization’s Flock network by any agency in the Flock System.

For items 1 and 2, please provide all maintained and exportable fields, including, where present, search timestamps, user names and identifiers, organization names and identifiers, search reasons, complaint or case numbers, search types, filters, date ranges searched, and counts of networks or devices searched. The reasons for a search, associated complaint number, and identity of the authorized inquirer are specifically addressed by General Order O-12.5, "Operation."

3. Existing electronic records of the Department's inbound and outbound Flock network-sharing configuration as of the date the search for these records is conducted. Include the names and identifiers of organizations sharing their networks with the Department and organizations with which the Department shares its networks, together with the direction and status of each sharing relationship. Please provide existing settings exports or reports, or the underlying electronically retrievable configuration records in an available format.

4. Flock Safety Event Log.
For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: the Flock Safety Event Log, including all maintained and exportable fields. Per Flock's documentation, the Event Log is available within the Insights tab. Flock customer support may be able to assist with the mass-downloading of this data if assistance is required.

The Organization Audit, Network Audit, and Event Log are identified by their Flock report names and their availability through the Insights tab. If these reports have been renamed or moved, please provide the equivalent records. Items 1, 2, and 4 seek audit and event records, rather than a bulk export of the underlying vehicle-sighting database or camera images.

Records relating to the Department's ALPR policy:

5.  All versions of written policies governing the deployment of automated license plate recognition cameras/readers/systems and the use, storage, retention, and sharing of data obtained through those systems that were created, revised, or in effect at any time from January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed. Include General Order O-12.5, applicable predecessor policies, amendments, and existing records showing each version's effective date and review date. Include policies adopted before January 1, 2024 if they remained in effect during any part of the requested period.

6. For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: all records of completed audits of ALPR system usage, data access, and hit-verification procedures, including any audit reports, findings, worksheets, spreadsheets, checklists, reviewer notes, sampling methodology, and corrective-action recommendations. This includes records of the regular audits required by General Order O-12.5, "Auditing and Oversight," and corresponding audits conducted under predecessor ALPR policies. This item seeks records of completed compliance audits and reviews, distinct from the underlying automated logs requested in items 1, 2, and 4.

7. All completed Memoranda of Understanding and data-sharing agreements governing the Department's sharing of ALPR data with other law enforcement agencies that were executed, amended, or in effect at any time from January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed. Include agreements completed or electronically accepted within the Flock system, amendments, and any execution or acceptance records maintained with those agreements. Include agreements executed before January 1, 2024 if they remained in effect during any part of the requested period. This includes the agreements required by General Order O-12.5, "Releasing ALPR Data," which provides that a formal MOU or data-sharing agreement will be completed within the Flock system when ALPR data is shared with other law enforcement agencies.

8. For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: all existing records concerning initial and refresher ALPR training provided to Department personnel, including Department-conducted and vendor-provided workshops, meetings, demonstrations, webinars, and other training sessions. This includes meeting notices and invitations, schedules, agendas, session dates and locations, instructor and training-provider information, registration records, attendance rosters, sign-in sheets, completion records and certificates, lesson plans, curricula, presentations, handouts, training bulletins, and any retained recordings. The request includes training on operation and configuration of the ALPR system, access to and use of ALPR data, Department policy and procedures, applicable laws, privacy protections, and verification of ALPR hits, as addressed by General Order O-12.5, "Training," and corresponding training under predecessor ALPR policies. Include existing records of Department approval of those training programs and refresher training addressing system updates, changes in law, or policy revisions.

9. For the period January 1, 2024 to the date this request is processed: all Department communications, including email and attachments, containing at least one keyword or phrase from each of the following two groups, matched without regard to capitalization:
(a) "ALPR," "ALPRs," "LPR," "LPRs," "Flock," "FlockOS," "Axon," "license plate reader," "license plate readers," or "license plate recognition";  AND (b) "audit," "audits," "audited," "auditing," "inspect," "inspected," "inspection," "inspections," "compliance," "policy violation," "policy violations," "unauthorized," "abuse," or "misuse."

This request seeks existing retained records, including responsive records maintained in Flock or another service on the Department's behalf. It does not ask the Department to create new policies, agreements, audit findings, training records, or narrative summaries. Where no pre-compiled report exists, please retrieve or extract existing electronic records or data that can be retrieved with reasonable effort, as provided by Public Officers Law Section 89(3)(a).

Please provide records electronically in their native or existing machine-readable export format where available. For tabular audit, event, and configuration records, CSV or spreadsheet files are preferred to PDF printouts or screenshots. Please retain column headings and timestamps as maintained. For other records, please provide the existing electronic files, including responsive email attachments.

If any record or portion is withheld, please identify the specific statutory exemption relied upon, explain its application, and disclose all reasonably segregable nonexempt portions. If particular entries or fields in an audit or event log are properly exempt, please redact those portions rather than withhold the entire report.

Please address each numbered item separately. For records the Department does not possess or cannot locate after a diligent search, please provide the certification contemplated by Public Officers Law Section 89(3)(a), identifying the relevant request item.

Please provide responsive records on a rolling basis as they become available and advise me in advance of any proposed charges.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 5 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Scott Conway
